name: AutoSubSync
description: Automatically synchronizes external and embedded subtitles across your library, aligning each one against the audio of the media it belongs to. The sync engine is downloaded once on first use and verified against a checksum built into the plugin.
overview: Automatically synchronizes external and embedded subtitles across your library.

versions.changelog: Subtitles that carry a marker cue at the start are no longer rejected for a shift that never happened; the offset is now measured from the cues themselves rather than from the position of the first one, and rejections made by the old measurement are re-checked automatically after upgrading. The same subtitle can no longer be synced twice at once by a scan and a library event, a subtitle whose OCR failed is no longer retried on every scan, and identical subtitle files on one item are now measured once instead of costing an engine run each.

Duplicate removal no longer deletes a subtitle as a duplicate of itself, and a subtitle removed as a duplicate is no longer retried and reported failed on every scan. Settings now apply to what has already been processed: lowering the minimum offset retries what it skipped, raising the maximum retries what it rejected, and changing an output setting reprocesses the subtitles it would have changed. Refreshing an item no longer re-runs subtitles that have not changed, and VobSub tracks identified by their .idx file are now recognized and can be converted with OCR.

The full library scan now syncs several subtitles at once, governed by Concurrent syncs, and automatic concurrency measures how much work actually completes instead of trusting the permit. Each sync is pinned to one CPU thread so the core budget means what it says. Framerate corrections up to 30% are no longer rejected as over-large shifts, Maximum offset now defaults to 60 seconds and measures the shift only, and every sync logs how far it moved the subtitle.

Subtitles are now aligned by ffsubsync alone; the engine fallback chain and its setting are gone. Adds a Maximum offset setting that rejects a result moving a subtitle further than you allow, raises the Minimum offset default to 150 ms, detects hearing-impaired tracks by their content rather than only their flag, and reports MicroDVD .sub files as unsupported.
